title: Failure needle-in-haystack catalog and oncall signal playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Build a unified failure catalog and an oncall playbook that makes a single-pane error dashboard and taxonomy to help engineers find the "needle" — the root cause — across timeouts, overload, model errors, and transport codes (HTTP/gRPC).

Background: We have multiple dashboards and ad-hoc tags across runtime, api-gateway, and model adapters. Oncall frequently toggles between traces, raw logs, and per-service dashboards to determine whether an incident is controller overload, kernel OOM, model rejection, or transient network problems. Existing dashboards surface counts but not the canonical failure classification or an automated first-pass attribution.

Goals:
- Define a compact failure taxonomy and canonical enrichments emitted by tracing hooks and metric/log pipelines.
- Ship a dashboard that surfaces aggregated failure slices (timeouts, overload, model-failure, http/grpc codes) with clear drilldowns to traces and suggested runbook steps.
- Provide an oncall signal playbook that recommends next steps and triage commands based on taxonomy.

Non-goals:
- Replacing full SRE incident automation.
- Doing model-level debugging; we only add pointers (model id, model-claim, rejection reason).

Design summary:
1) Taxonomy: top-level classes = {Timeout, Overload, ModelError, TransportError, ClientInputError, InternalRuntime}. Each failure event carries subtype tags (e.g., KV_CACHE_MISS, KERNEL_OOM, SOFT_QUOTA, MODEL_REJECT, RESPONSE_TRUNCATION).
2) Enrichment fields to emit on traces/metrics/logs: failure_class, failure_subtype, inferred_slo_breach (boolean), primary_http_status, primary_grpc_code, model_id, model_variant, latency_ms, serving_pool, host_pool, request_bucket. These will be emitted as deterministic string tags on the root span and as metric labels for counters/histograms.
3) Tracing hooks: add a lightweight failure-classifier middleware in runtime that runs at span end. Rules are ordered: explicit model rejection (gRPC/JSON model error) -> kernel OOM / runtime exit -> deadline/response timeout -> circuit-breaker/queue overflow -> transport (http/gRPC non-200 non-OK codes) -> fallback to generic InternalRuntime. The middleware attaches failure tags and a short diagnostic snippet (first 256 chars of model error or kernel message).
4) Metrics/log pipeline: populate new Prometheus counters and histograms: infra_failure_count{failure_class,failure_subtype,host_pool}, request_latency_bucket_ms{failure_class,model_id}, failure_rate_by_model, transport_error_count{http_status,grpc_code}. Logs to be forwarded with structured JSON fields to ELK/Datadog and separate index for failure-events.
5) Dashboard UX: top-left SLO health sparkline, center failure-class distribution and trend (7d/1d), right-side drilldowns listing top traces-per-failure-subtype with direct link to trace id and runtime PR that changed recent kernel logic. Provide a one-click "Runbook" button that surfaces the recommended triage play for the dominant failure subtype.

Acceptance criteria:
- At least 90% of production incidents that were classified manually over the past 90 days are assigned the same top-level failure_class by the automated classifier (sample-based verification).
- Dashboard shows failure_class trend with usable trace links and query times under 2s for common slices.
- Oncall playbook entries created for each top-level class with at least one actionable command.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): instrument tracing hooks in canary runtime pool, emit tags to a non-prod telemetry index, validate tag coverage and cardinality.
- Phase 2 (pilot customers): enable on a small subset of production traffic for 48h, collect mismatch metrics between automated classifier and human annotations.
- Phase 3: full rollout with dashboards enabled and alerts mapped.

Monitoring & alerts:
- New alert: Rapid spike in failure_rate_by_model > 3x baseline for 5m -> page oncall and attach classification summary.
- New alert: classifier drop below 80% sampling agreement with human annotations during pilot -> open internal ticket for investigation.

Open questions:
- Cardinality controls: which model_id dimensions should be whitelisted to avoid explosion? Proposal: only report model_id at 1h sampling for high-cardinality customers unless opt-in.
- How to represent multi-cause failures (e.g., overloaded host leading to model timeouts)? Current plan: primary_cause + secondary_tags list (secondary_tags is a comma-separated string).

Next steps:
- Finalize the classifier rule table and unit tests (owner: Jonah).
- Create Prometheus metric names and test metric export from canary (owner: Priya Patel).
- Create dashboard wireframe and add links to the runtime PR and playbook pages (owner: Ava).

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Failure+Needle+Catalog+Design
- Dev PR (runtime classifier): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/obs/failure-needle-catalog-proto

Notes on trade-offs:
- We prioritize low-latency classification in tracing hooks and thus limit expensive checks (no model-level full logs). Deeper model debugging will remain off-platform to avoid telemetry cost.
- We keep failure_class values intentionally small and stable to avoid churn in dashboards and alerts.
comments: 2025-01-11 - Jonah Kim: Initial spike of work done. Added end-to-end tests for rule ordering. Need to add stable mapping for http -> TransportError. Next: add prometheus exporter unit tests.

2025-01-13 - Priya Patel: Reviewed metric names. Suggested collapsing kernel-related subtypes to reduce cardinality: KERNEL_OOM -> KERNEL_RESOURCE. Also recommended whitelisting model_id only for enterprise customers (agreed).

2025-01-15 - SRE Review (Liam Nguyen): Saw good coverage of timeout cases. Raised concern about adding diagnostic snippets to span root due to PII risk. Action: redact user input and truncate to 256 chars.
